Thanks Hannah — couple clarifying questions before you run the bench:

1) For p95/p99 numbers: are you reporting single-request latency (cold start excluded) or end-to-end including model load and KV cache effects? We care about sustained interactive latency.
2) Concurrency: our target is ~120 concurrent users during peak (roughly 40 QPS). Can you include a run that simulates concurrency to show tail behavior?
3) Tokens per response: average ~180 tokens, but we can vary. Can you include a 300-token scenario?

If you can include those variants that would be ideal. ETA?

—Alex
Alex Johnson

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 10:15 AM Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novacorp.com> wrote:
> 1) For p95/p99 numbers: are you reporting single-request latency (cold start excluded) or end-to-end including model load and KV cache effects?
> 2) Concurrency: our target is ~120 concurrent users during peak (roughly 40 QPS). Can you include a run that simulates concurrency to show tail behavior?
> 3) Tokens per response: average ~180 tokens, but we can vary. Can you include a 300-token scenario?

Thanks for the clear list — ran three focused runs and attached the summary + raw CSVs. Short answers up front:
- Latency reported: steady-state single-request latency (model already loaded, KV cache warmed) but we also captured simulated cold-start events in a separate run. See bench table in attached PDF.
- Concurrency: simulated 50, 100, and 150 concurrent connections (sustained) with a 95th/99th tail measurement. At 100 concurrent we saw p95 = 210ms, p99 = 410ms for the 180-token configuration; at 150 concurrent p95 = 270ms, p99 = 630ms.
- 300-token responses: p95 and p99 increased ~1.5x relative to 180-token baseline (see row \"300t-concur-100\" in CSV).

Files attached: redwood_bench_report.pdf (summary + charts), novacorp_perf_summary.csv (raw rows). Quick recommendation: if NovaCorp wants p99 < 500ms at 100 concurrent for 300-token responses we recommend Dedicated slot with the performance profile M-8 and the optional KV cache warmers enabled.

Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the CSV if useful.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
